title: WASSCE Components of Mobile Phone - Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1 - Hardware Components
subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: What does PCB stand for in the context of mobile phone hardware?
questions.explain: The PCB is the foundational board where all other hardware components are mounted and interconnected.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: On a mobile phone's Printed Circuit Board (PCB), what is the primary purpose of the copper tracks or traces?
options: To provide physical support to the battery.
To act as the main processor for the OS.
To conduct electrical signals and power between different components.
questions.explain: Traces are etched onto the PCB to act as wiring, electrically connecting components like resistors, ICs, and the battery.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Modern mobile phone PCBs use a multilayer architecture. Which of the following best describes why a multilayer PCB is essential in GSM repair contexts?
options: It allows the phone to bend without breaking.
It provides independent layers for signal routing, ground, and power, enabling compact designs.
It prevents the software applications from accessing the firmware.
It replaces the need for an internal battery by storing static charge.
questions.explain: Due to the complex block diagram (Power, Memory, RF, Audio units), multilayer PCBs are required to fit intricate routing in a tiny form factor.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which basic hardware component is primarily designed to oppose the flow of electrical current in a mobile phone's circuit?
questions.explain: A resistor's main function is to restrict or oppose the flow of electrical current, helping to manage voltage levels across the board.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: If a Surface Mount Device (SMD) resistor on a PCB is marked '223', what is its expected resistance value? Note: Resistance $R$ relies on a multiplier based on the last digit ($10^x$).
questions.explain: A '223' SMD code means 22 followed by 3 zeros ($22 \times 10^3$), which equals 22,000 ohms or 22k ohms.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: In a mobile phone's power management circuit, transistors are frequently utilized. Which of the following is a primary function of a transistor in this specific context?
options: To permanently store the operating system files.
To capture audio from the environment.
To act as an electronic switch to route power from the battery to various ICs.
To transmit radio frequencies to the cellular tower.
questions.explain: Transistors in mobile phones primarily function as high-speed switches or amplifiers, essential for routing power within the Power unit.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which component allows electrical current to flow easily in only one direction, providing protection against reverse polarity?
questions.explain: A diode functions as a one-way valve for electrical current, commonly used to protect circuits from improper battery insertion (reverse polarity).
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which specialized type of diode is heavily used in a mobile phone's charging section to regulate voltage and protect components from voltage spikes?
questions.explain: Zener diodes are unique because they permit current to flow in the reverse direction when a specific voltage is reached, making them perfect for voltage regulation.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Integrated Circuits (ICs) in modern mobile phones are predominantly surface-mounted. What does the acronym BGA stand for regarding IC packaging?
questions.explain: Most major ICs like the CPU and Memory use Ball Grid Array (BGA) packaging to save space on the PCB.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which electronic component stores an electrical charge temporarily and is widely used for filtering in a mobile phone's circuitry?
questions.explain: Capacitors store electrical energy in an electric field and are crucial for smoothing out power supply fluctuations (filtering).
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: When diagnosing a motherboard, you find a capacitor connected in parallel with the power line to the ground. What is its likely function?
options: To act as a decoupling capacitor, stabilizing the power supply to an IC.
To convert analog audio into digital signals.
To block Direct Current (DC) while passing Alternating Current (AC) between stages.
questions.explain: Capacitors in parallel with power lines are decoupling (or bypass) capacitors, preventing voltage drops and noise from affecting the IC.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which component is strictly responsible for capturing acoustic sound waves and turning them into an electrical analog signal?
questions.explain: The microphone acts as a transducer, converting external acoustic sound into electrical signals.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: In mobile phone architecture, how does the 'Speaker' (hands-free) differ fundamentally from the 'Earpiece' (Receiver)?
options: The speaker inputs sound, while the earpiece outputs sound.
The speaker outputs high-volume audio like ringtones, while the earpiece outputs low-volume audio for private calls.
The speaker connects to the RF unit, while the earpiece connects to the Power unit.
The earpiece requires an ADC, while the speaker requires an antenna.
questions.explain: A speaker (ringer/buzzer) drives loud audio, while the earpiece (receiver) is a smaller speaker intended for the user's ear during a call.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: What is the primary function of the battery in a mobile phone?
options: To provide the essential Direct Current (DC) voltage required to run the device.
To capture the user's audio input.
questions.explain: The battery serves as the fundamental, portable energy source, supplying DC power to the PCB and its components.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Most modern smartphone batteries are based on which specific chemical technology due to its high energy density and lightweight properties?
questions.explain: Li-ion and Li-Po batteries dominate the modern mobile phone industry because they pack high energy capacity without the 'memory effect'.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which component is tasked with radiating and receiving electromagnetic waves to communicate with cellular towers?
questions.explain: The antenna bridges the internal circuitry and external free space, receiving and transmitting radio waves.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: What does the acronym LCD stand for in mobile phone screen technology?
questions.explain: LCD stands for Liquid Crystal Display, a flat-panel display technology relying on the light-modulating properties of liquid crystals.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: When comparing screen technologies, what is a fundamental operational difference between an LCD and an OLED screen in a mobile phone?
options: OLED requires a separate backlight panel, while LCD does not.
LCDs are entirely software-driven, while OLEDs are entirely hardware-driven.
OLED pixels emit their own light (self-illuminating), whereas LCD pixels require a backlight.
LCD displays cannot show colors, while OLED displays can.
questions.explain: OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) pixels are self-illuminating, which provides absolute blacks and removes the need for the bulky backlight assembly found in LCDs.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: When troubleshooting a completely dark LCD (though the phone is actively receiving calls), a technician suspects a backlight failure. Which hardware component in the display driver circuit is uniquely responsible for stepping up the battery voltage ($~3.7V$) to the high voltage ($>15V$) needed for the LCD backlight string?
questions.explain: The backlight driver IC relies on an inductor (boost coil) to step up the low battery voltage to the high voltage required to light up the LCD's LED strip.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: A specialized resistor is often incorporated directly into the battery pack or charging circuit. Its resistance changes significantly with temperature to prevent thermal runaway. What is this component called?
questions.explain: A thermistor (thermal resistor) tracks battery temperature. If the battery overheats while charging, its resistance changes to signal the Power IC to halt charging.
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1
